rationale: Toronto entry list (Jul 8) has 9 of the top 10, and world No.1 Sabalenka is entered (she skipped Canada in 2025) with a 23-1 hard-court record in 2026 and the Sunshine Double. Defending champion Mboko (Jul 7, knee) and Wimbledon finalist Muchova (Jul 18, surgery) withdrew; the draw is Jul 31 and the event runs Aug 2-13.

RFEF assembly (Jun 30): Saudi is out for Feb 5-7 2027 because of the Asian Cup, with proposals but 'no firm offers'. Marca-based reports (Jul 18-19) list Mexico (formal FMF bid), the US, Egypt, China and Qatar, and say Qatar's bid is weakened by regional security after the Iran war resumed Jul 15. A decision is expected 'in the coming months' (the 2026 venue was only announced Sep 29), so an announcement before Aug 31 is uncertain.

Australia named a full-strength attack on Jul 21 (Cummins, Hazlewood, Starc, Lyon, Boland) for Darwin Aug 13-17. Bangladesh's squad is not yet named; the last Test squad (vs Zimbabwe, late June) was led by Shanto and lacked Litton (calf strain), who is likely back. Bangladesh were bowled out for 140 in Harare with Mominul top-scoring on 60.

Nashville beat Atlanta 1-0 on Jul 17 and lead the East and the Supporters' Shield on 36 pts from 15 games. Miami are 2nd on 31 from 15 (Miami Herald, Jul 21), and Messi and De Paul are on vacation after the WC final, likely missing three MLS games until the Leagues Cup (Aug 5). Only about 4-6 games each remain before Aug 19.

The deadliest 2026 quake is still the Jun 16 Sigi M6.7 in Central Sulawesi (3 deaths per BNPB). The Apr 2 M7.6 Molucca Sea quake killed 1 in Manado, Jul 3 North Maluku M6.2 had no casualties, Jul 12 Buol (also Central Sulawesi) killed 1, and Jul 19 Sukabumi M5.0 caused no damage. Only about 27 days remain for a deadlier quake elsewhere.

Harris (2025 world champion) set the 2026 world lead of 24.08 at the Australian trials (Jun 13). Shayna Jack retires after the Commonwealth Games and skips Pan Pacs, and Perkins was 3rd in 24.63. I found no new 2026 times for the US sprinters (Walsh, Huske), and Pan Pacs is at home in Irvine for the US.

UFC 330 (Aug 15, Philadelphia) co-main confirmed Jul 1. Opening odds ranged from Dern -120/Robertson +100 (DraftKings) to -188/+146 (FanDuel) and -210/+180 (BetOnline), about 62% for Dern no-vig. Dern stays champion if the bout falls through, and Robertson is on a 5-fight win streak.

Alcaraz (defending champion) entered Cincinnati (Aug 13-23) on Jul 16 for his return from a wrist injury, and Sinner is also entered. That raises the chance that a deep Djokovic run ends against one of them; Sinner beat Djokovic easily in the Wimbledon SF (Jul 10). Early-round losers remain unpredictable until the draw (~Aug 11).

UFC 330 main event confirmed (Jul 1). Makhachev opened at -365 and Garry at +300 (BetOnline, Jun 18), about 76% for Makhachev no-vig. There is a small extra risk of an opponent change or an interim-title scenario.

McIntosh swam only four events at the Canadian trials (Jul 5-8: 200 fly, 400 IM, 400 free, 200 IM, 'down from five'), dropping the 800 free, so she likely skips it at Pan Pacs. Pallister (8:05.98, 0.36s behind Ledecky at the 2025 Worlds) won the 400, 800 and 1500 at the Australian trials in June 'in super-quick times'. Ledecky beat McIntosh head-to-head in March 2026 (8:08.57).

Arsenal (PL champions) v Manchester City (FA Cup winners) at Wembley on Aug 16 is Maresca's first competitive game for City (Jun 29). It is close to a coin flip with penalties if level; no new form or injury news found.

Groups (BBC, Jul 21): A Morocco/Algeria/Senegal/Kenya, B South Africa/Ivory Coast/Burkina Faso/Tanzania, C Nigeria/Zambia/Egypt/Malawi, D Ghana/Cameroon/Mali/Cape Verde. Holders and top-ranked Nigeria and hosts Morocco (runners-up in 2022 and 2025, coached by Vilda) are the favourites, with South Africa, Ghana and Zambia next.

Scheffler is still No.1 but winless since January, with many top-4 finishes and a missed cut at the Scottish Open (Jul 10). Ryan Fox won the Open (Jul 19) with Cameron Young close behind. The field is very open and odds aren't out until the week of Aug 10.

India finished 8th of 9 in the Pro League (W4 D5 L7; squad named Jul 21) and drew 2-2 with England before losing the shootout 1-4 (Jun 25). England 'finished really well' to avoid relegation (Jul 15). Pakistan were last and lost 7-1 to India. Pool D in Amstelveen: India v England on Aug 17, India v Pakistan on Aug 19.
